findings: Re-verified all four verdicts against title plus body. The central claim is carried twice over: the title says 大規模な不正は「確認できていない」 and the body says 「そうした主張を証明するものは何も見つかっていない」.

「1日」 occurs exactly once in the whole record and belongs to Georgia official Sterling (「ゲイブリエル・スターリング氏は1日」); the record gives Barr's remark no date at all, so NOT_IN_SOURCE is right and CONTRADICTED would overreach.
「ドナルド・トランプ大統領の主張」 against the body's 「トランプ氏側の主張」 is not an entity substitution: the body also has Trump himself reasserting the fraud claim on Twitter.
Arithmetic 47+20+15+5=87 and GOOD (75-89) both hold; coverage 20 is fair for one sentence that carries the main finding but drops the AP setting and every reaction.
All seven verdicts reproduce from the source: 「バー氏は今回のAP通信の取材で」, 「トランプ氏に特に近い側近の1人とみられているバー氏」, 「大統領選での敗北を受け入れていないトランプ氏にとって、大きな打撃となるとみられる」, 「ルディ・ジュリアーニ弁護士とジェナ・エリス弁護士は共同声明を発表」.

One fidelity slip the Scorer did not list: the Schumer line is quoted as 「次にクビにされるのは彼だろう」 while the record reads 「次にクビにされるのはおそらく彼だろう」, so the hedge is dropped inside quotation marks. It hardens the prediction slightly but contradicts nothing.

The undated 「1日」 is the same defect as in 0166e910 and is scored identically at faithfulness 47, so the trace is internally consistent; no CONTRADICTED claim exists, so the automatic-revise rule does not apply.

47+28+15+5=95 and EXCELLENT (90-100) hold. Coverage 28 is the generous edge (the Justice Department's 「捜査が終了したわけはなく」 line is missing); my independent range of 45-47 and 26-28 spans 91-95, so the band cannot move and I approve rather than replace.
Both CONTRADICTED verdicts confirmed by independent counting: 「記者会見」 appears nowhere in the record while 「AP通信」 appears twice, and 「個別」 appears nowhere against the body's 「そうした主張を証明するものは何も見つかっていない」.
The invented second finding is genuinely invented, not merely uncited: the only forward-looking line is the spokesman's promise to pursue 「具体的で信憑性のある不正の疑い」, which is not a report of confirmed fraud.

Deliberately checked for escalation and rejected it: sentence 1 states the central finding correctly and sentence 2 itself concedes 「選挙結果を左右しない規模」, so the central outcome is not reversed and the rubric keeps an invented secondary sub-claim inside soft scoring.
Faithfulness 23 sits below 40, so the automatic-revise rule for CONTRADICTED claims does not fire; 23+22+14+5=64 and MIXED (50-64) hold.
Both CONTRADICTED verdicts confirmed by counting the record: 「メディケイド」 occurs 7 times and 「メディケア」 0; 「８割」 occurs once and 「9割」/「九割」 0.

No escalation: the misnamed programme still denotes the same lifeline the article describes (「オバマ政権時代に拡大されたメディケイド（低所得者向け公的医療保険）」), and the central event - expanded Medicaid supporting patients while Republicans weigh deep cuts - survives intact, which is exactly the wrong-secondary-entity case the rubric keeps in soft scoring.
Faithfulness 24 is below 40, so the CONTRADICTED rule does not fire; 24+20+15+5=64 and MIXED hold.
Coverage 20 here against 23 for the otherwise identical 964b4aa4 is defensible rather than inconsistent: a misnamed programme delivers less of the key fact it is supposed to carry.

The candidate physically stops mid-word at 「しかしそ」. Coherence 3/15 matches the rubric's incoherence floor and coverage 6 correctly reflects that no main-event content survives: Medicaid, the Republican cuts, the doctor and his patients are all absent.

Nothing asserted is false. 「ほとんどの炭鉱が閉山に追い込まれた今、アパラチア山脈に暮らす人たちの選択肢はほかにあまりない」 and 「レッチャー郡では８割の有権者が同氏を選び」 carry the two standing claims, so faithfulness 44 with one unverifiable fragment is in range; 44+6+3+4=57 and MIXED hold.

Observation for the funnel owner, not a decision I can take in this pass: a cut in mid-word is stronger evidence of physical truncation than the rubric's particle-ending caveat, so this candidate arguably belonged to the OBVIOUS_TRUNCATION hard gate upstream (score 0, terminal_rank 2). That is a Layer-1 call, and the soft-score pass admits only FACTUAL_REVERSAL and FABRICATED_CONTENT escalations, so I leave the soft score standing.
The Scorer's issue note that 'no terminal category is proposed for it per the rubric' is loose wording - the rubric does have a truncation terminal - but it does not affect any number here.
「ここから800キロ離れたワシントンで下される決定が、重大な影響を及ぼすかもしれない」 supports the Washington claim, and 何百キロ is a faithful rendering of 800キロ.

「今後数週間」 appears nowhere in the record; the only horizon in it is 「今後数年」 inside a resident's quote about premiums, a different subject, so NOT_IN_SOURCE rather than CONTRADICTED is the correct verdict.
45+10+14+5=74 and FINE (65-74) hold, at the top of the band. Coverage 10 correctly reflects an opening tease that never names healthcare, Medicaid or the Republican cuts.

All four verdicts reproduce, including 「レッチャー郡では８割の有権者が同氏を選び」 and 「オバマ政権時代に拡大されたメディケイド（低所得者向け公的医療保険）」; attributing the expansion to オバマケア is consistent with the record, which presents オバマ氏の医療保険制度改革 as its source.

The attribution stretch the Scorer flagged is real: the 命綱 framing belongs to patient Lucas (「メディケイドのおかげで命拾いした」) and the doctor's alarm is shown indirectly, so faithfulness 48 prices it at only -2, lighter than the -3 and -4 this batch charges for an invented date and an invented town.

48+23+15+5=91 sits two points inside EXCELLENT. My independent range (faithfulness 46-48, coverage 21-24, given the omitted opioid programme and the premium-rise counter-voice) spans 87-92, so the label is genuinely boundary-sensitive.
I approve rather than substitute because every dimension is individually defensible and the arithmetic and band mapping are correct; recorded here so the boundary sensitivity stays in the trace.
The headline finding reproduces twice: 「英国の男の子がサッカー選手やYouTubeスターになりたがるのに対し、ウガンダやザンビアでは医師や教師になりたいという子が多い」 and 「英国以外の国では、苦しい生活にもかかわらず高い志を表す絵が目立った」.
「高等教育」 is absent from the record, so charging the gloss 3 faithfulness points is reasonable; doctor and teacher entail it, which is why it is a gloss and not a contradiction.
47+15+15+5=82 and GOOD hold. Coverage 15 for one sentence that omits the 20-country / 20,000-child scale, the gender-stereotype result and every expert comment is fair.

Both quotations reproduce verbatim from the record and both attributions are correct, including that Cruickshank chairs the very charity that ran the survey (「同氏は、調査を実施した慈善団体「Education and Employers」の理事長でもある」).

Coverage 5/30 correctly captures the defect: the summary reports reactions to a finding it never states, so the reader learns a 「結果」 was meaningful without learning what it was. This is the same shape as the rubric's low-coverage reference case, which also lands in FINE.
50+5+13+4=72 and FINE (65-74) hold; faithfulness 50 is warranted because nothing asserted departs from the source.

Checked and cleared for copying: both sentences restate two non-adjacent article sentences with the quotations intact, which the rubric classes as ordinary quotation overlap, not continuous high-coverage copying, so VERBATIM_SOURCE_COPY is correctly not in play.

All seven verdicts reproduce: 「2万人の子供を対象に調査を実施した」, 「世界20カ国で7歳から11歳の小学生に」, the UK boys' football/YouTube line, 「英国の女の子が憧れる職業の上位10種類には、看護師、ダンサー、美容師などが含まれた」, 「性別による役割のステレオタイプが固まってしまうかを示す結果」 and 「幼少期から多様な職種に触れさせる必要があることが調査から分かった」.

The 途上国-versus-英国 generalization is stated at the record's own level of generality (its English headline line is 'Children in poorer countries have higher career aspirations than UK'), so SUPPORTED holds even though UK girls also favour teacher and doctor.
50+27+15+5=97 and EXCELLENT hold.

Trace inconsistency, label-neutral: 「高等教育を要する専門職」 carries no faithfulness deduction here while the near-identical gloss costs 519dda6a 3 points. Correcting in either direction (47 here gives 94, or 50 there gives 85) leaves both labels unchanged, so I flag the calibration rather than replace numbers.

オハイオ州 is carried by the record's own English-headline line ('Ohio dad makes girl walk miles to school for bullying on bus'), which is part of the article text, so SUPPORTED is right and not a fabrication.
「スワントン」 appears nowhere in title or body, so NOT_IN_SOURCE is correct; the walk claim is supported by 「合計8キロの距離は、カーステンさんがスクールバスの利用を禁止された3日間の間、数回に分けて歩ききった」.
46+22+15+5=88 and GOOD (75-89) hold; a 4-point charge for one invented town with everything else accurate is proportionate.
Same four verdicts as 381886c7, and faithfulness 46 / coverage 22 are correctly held constant because the content is identical - only the sentence order differs.

The ordering defect is real and correctly identified: 「父親がビデオを投稿したのを機に…」 arrives before the father, the daughter or the walk are introduced, so both 「父親」 and 「このしつけ方法」 dangle and the effect precedes its cause.
Coherence 7/15 is a defensible middle between fully fluent prose (15) and the rubric's scrambled-dependency floor (3); my independent range is 6-9, which does not move the band.
46+22+7+5=80 and GOOD (75-89) hold mechanically. Noting only that the GOOD label for an inverted-order summary rests entirely on that coherence figure.
All six verdicts reproduce, including 「娘がバスで他の生徒をいじめたと叱られたのはこれで2回目だった」, 「コックスさんは3日、初日のビデオをフェイスブックに投稿」, 「1700万回以上再生され」 and 「自分もいじめられたことがあり、今回のことで人に優しくすることを覚えた」.
Faithfulness 50 is warranted: nothing asserted departs from the record, and 「約8キロ」 is a faithful rendering of 「合計8キロ」.
50+27+15+5=97 and EXCELLENT hold; the only omissions are the three-day bus ban and the expert's caution about the 2-degree cold, which the Scorer documented.

The invented middle sentence is confirmed independently: 「称賛」 appears nowhere in the record, and the only television in it is 「地元テレビのWTVGニュースによると」 - a station reporting the story, not the father appearing on a programme; he spoke to 「地元メディアのニュース5クリーヴランド」.
NOT_IN_SOURCE rather than CONTRADICTED is right for both: the article never denies a TV appearance or school approval, it simply contains neither.

Escalation considered and rejected, and this is the closest call in the batch. The summary's message rests on the walk, the video and the split debate, all accurate, so the invented school endorsement is a secondary claim about reception, which the rubric's centrality test keeps inside soft scoring - even though it fills one of only three sentences and softens how the discipline was received.

22+24+14+4=64 and MIXED hold; faithfulness 22 for a wholly invented sentence is consistent with this batch's severity ordering (3-4 points for one invented detail, low twenties for an invented sentence).

All three verdicts reproduce: 「「Subtle Asian Traits」を立ち上げたのは、豪メルボルンに住む中国系オーストラリア人の高校生9人だ」, 「海外に住むアジア人に文化的な一大現象を巻き起こしている」 and 「9月の立ち上げから現在までに100万人近くが参加している」. Faithfulness 50 is warranted; dropping the count 9人 is an omission, not an error.
50+22+15+5=92 and EXCELLENT (90-100) hold.

Coverage 22 for a single sentence is the generous edge, since the article's second half - the cultural-identity dispute, the East-Asia-centric criticism and the stereotype debate - is entirely absent. My range of 20-23 keeps the score at 90-93, so the band does not move and I approve rather than replace.
Coverage 22 here against 15 for the one-sentence careers summary 519dda6a is justified: this candidate carries main event, founders and scale, where that one carries only the headline finding.

Both standing claims reproduce: 「（アジア発のこの人気ドリンクにまつわるジョークはたくさんある）」 and 「最初のアイデアは、単に家での生活やアジア文化の「ちょっと変わったところ」、バブルティーに関するネタやジョークを共有したかった」. 「頻繁に投稿されている」 is a mild extrapolation from 「たくさんある」, correctly priced at -3.
Coverage 4/30 correctly reflects a summary built on a parenthetical aside that never states the main event: no founders, no September launch, no near-million membership, no identity debate.
47+4+14+4=69 and FINE (65-74) hold. The rubric's additive design deliberately allows an accurate but near-contentless summary to land here, so the label is rubric-consistent rather than generous.
What is wrong is the faithfulness figure, not the structure of the review: 36/50 rests on one incorrect claim verdict and on double-charging a defect the Scorer had already assigned to coherence.

Incorrect verdict: 「ちょっとしたアジア人の特徴」 is marked NOT_IN_SOURCE, but it is a rendering of the group's own English name, which is in the record. It asserts nothing about the world beyond that name, so it should carry no faithfulness deduction at all.

Double-counting: the proposition that a photo was posted to this group is in fact supported - the record contains 「その後、母親から送られてきたというメッセージが下の写真だ」, a post that drew 「3万以上の「いいね」」. What fails is the deictic 「この写真」, which has no referent in the supplied text, and the Scorer already charged exactly that to coherence at 5/15 ('cannot stand alone without the image it points at').

Off this batch's own severity curve: 3 points for an invented date (0166e910), 4 for an invented town (381886c7), 28 for a wholly invented sentence (fc95363c). Charging 14 for two absent-but-not-false items is out of scale, and it is label-determining.

Replacement 42+2+5+5=54, so the label must be MIXED (50-64), not POOR. Coverage 2 and coherence 5 are correct and retained, conciseness 5 holds, and faithfulness 42 is set slightly below the 44-45 this batch gives a short candidate with one unverifiable element because here the unverifiable element is the subject of the only sentence.

The caption conveys no part of the main event, but the rubric's additive design deliberately lets a short, accurate, low-utility output score above 50 - its own low-coverage reference case reaches FINE - so POOR at 48 was reachable only through the over-harsh faithfulness figure.
No terminal: the group and its Facebook home are genuinely in the article, so neither OFF_TOPIC nor FABRICATED_CONTENT applies, and no escalation is warranted.
